summary: The diff implements ArrayBuffer.prototype.transferToFixedLength through a local ArrayBufferCopyAndDetach helper, with spec steps kept as comments in order. I found no defect. The order is right: RequireInternalSlot, then ToIndex (only when newLength is not undefined), then the detached check, then the resizability and detach-key checks, then AllocateArrayBuffer with the ? propagated, then the copy, then DetachArrayBuffer. Errors propagate with ?. There are no test-specific branches. The gate shows 18 new passes, no regressions, and the remaining failures are the expected not-implemented error from the separate resizable getter. Minor points only: step 2 (IsSharedArrayBuffer) is skipped on the stated basis that the engine has no shared data blocks, which I could not verify from the diff. Two defensive fallbacks (unwrap_or_default on the byte copy and unwrap_or(Undefined) on the detach key) would silently do the wrong thing if ever reached, although they look unreachable here.
notes_for_next_attempt: No changes required. Before merging, confirm that kahvi has no SharedArrayBuffer support that shares the ArrayBufferData slot. If it does, step 2 (throw TypeError when IsSharedArrayBuffer is true) must be implemented instead of skipped. Consider replacing the silent fallbacks (unwrap_or_default on the copied bytes in step 13, and unwrap_or(Value::Undefined) on the detach key in step 8) with an explicit internal-error path, since those states should be unreachable after the step-5 detached check.
